summary: Describes a URN namespace managed by SWIFT for use within messages that SWIFT standardizes for financial messaging. It registers the namespace so that identifiers can be written in a consistent, persistent form. It is a registration document and does not define a new protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo describes a URN namespace managed by SWIFT for financial message items. It explains how names are assigned, kept unique, and resolved.

questions: what is the swift urn namespace
how long are swift urns valid
subtitle: The SWIFT URN namespace for names used in financial messages.

tldr.problem: Financial messages need stable names for items such as schemas, even if a resource exists at more than one URL.
tldr.mechanism: The memo describes the swift URN namespace, whose names are assigned and resolved by SWIFT under its registration procedures.
tldr.outcome: The text says SWIFT names are not reassigned and are guaranteed to remain valid for 15 years.

today: RFC 3615 is an Informational description of the SWIFT URN namespace. Its text describes SWIFT as the responsible registrar and resolver.

sections.title: Stable Names for Financial Message Items
sections.content:
The memo says names for items in financial messages need to remain stable and unique, for example when identifying an XML schema. A single resource may have several physical locations and URLs but one URN.

SWIFT manages the namespace for use within messages standardized by SWIFT. The namespace is reserved to the global financial community.
sections.plainLanguage: A message item may move between locations but still needs one stable name. SWIFT defines a URN namespace for that purpose.

sections.title: The swift Namespace
sections.content:
The Namespace ID is swift. The namespace-specific string is a flat space with no structure that outsiders should infer or rely on.

SWIFT registration checks proposed names against those already assigned to ensure uniqueness. The RFC gives examples but says they are not guaranteed to be real identifiers.
sections.plainLanguage: Names begin with the swift namespace identifier. The rest should be treated as opaque rather than decoded by outside applications.

sections.title: Persistence, Resolution, and Registration
sections.content:
SWIFT's assignment process does not reassign names and guarantees that SWIFT URNs remain valid for 15 years. Names are granted through SWIFT's proprietary registration procedures.

Resolvers run under SWIFT's responsibility. The RFC says resolving a SWIFT URN through another resolver is error-prone and not authoritative, and records IANA's registration of URN namespace 15 to SWIFT.
sections.plainLanguage: SWIFT assigns and resolves the identifiers. The memo promises that names are not reused and remain valid for 15 years.

references.text: Daigle, L., van Gulik, D., Iannella, R. and P. Faltstrom, "Uniform Resource Name (URN) Namespace Definition Mechanisms", BCP 66, RFC 3406, October 2002.
